To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of SP, NKA and CGRP immunoractivities are significantly elevated in the dorsal and ventral cutaneous tissues of the early neonatal rat, compared with other developmental groups.
the levels of substance P and calcitonin-gene-related peptide in rat skin are elevated at birth.
the levels of SP, CGRP, NKA and PHI immunoreactivity in dorsal and ventural abdominal rat skin do not change significantly at various stages of rat development from foetal to adult.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ontogenic changes in neuropeptides in the primary sensory neurone in rat skin.
the ontogeny of the sensory innervation of the skin.
the ontogenic changes in neuropeptide concentrations in the skin and the possible role of these peptides in the control of cutaneous sensation in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the concentrations of SP and CGRPs in the rat dorsal skin are significantly elevated in early neonatal development.

the levels of SP, NKA and CGRP immunofluorescence in the dorsal and ventral rat skin remain relatively constant throughout development, with the exception of an early post-natal rise in the levels of SP- and CGRP-immunofluorescence.
there is no significant ontogenic change in the tissue concentrations, of the primary afferent neuropeptides, in the rat dorsal abdominal skin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neuropeptide concentrations in the skin of the rat change significantly during development and that this may be related to the development of the sensory innervation of the skin.

the concentrations of SP, NKA, CGRP and PHI immunoreactivities in dorsal and ventro abdominal skin are similar in adult and early neonatal rats, but that the levels of SP, NAK and CGRP immunoneactivities are elevated in early neonatal rats.

the neuropeptides in the primary sensory neurone in rat skin are present at a very early stage of development and that the concentrations of these peptides do not change significantly during development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the levels of CGRP immunoreactive peptide are elevated in neonatal skin and that the levels of SP are elevated in both neonatal and adult skin.

the neuropeptides of the sensory nerves are not only present in the skin of the rat, but they are present in the skin at a time when these neuropeptides may be important for the survival of the neonate.
there are ontogenic changes in neuropeptides in rat skin.
